notes: National 1,400 MW (2025) is C&W Global Market Comparison 2026 as summarised by a secondary site; the primary C&W page only gives Sydney 917 MW operational H1 2026 (+17%). CBRE Q1 2026: Sydney 950 MW live, Melbourne 580 MW live (1,530 MW combined); Knight Frank Q2 2026: Melbourne 443 MW live IT. UC figure is NEXTDC alone (ASX FY26, 27 Aug 2026: built 288 MW, under construction 537 MW, 197 MW activating in FY27), so national UC is higher. Planned 21,600 MW is the C&W national pipeline (16,800 MW early stage). UC UPDATE (2026-09-03): 243 MW = Sydney 116 MW + Melbourne 127 MW; this is our own aggregation (T5), not a stated national figure. Sydney 116 MW is derived from C&W's H1 2026 release (https://www.cushmanwakefield.com/en/singapore/news/2026/08/apac-dc-h1-2026): Sydney development pipeline 2,134 MW minus planned 2,018 MW, using C&W's own definition that pipeline = under construction + planned (26.5 GW = 4.8 + 21.7); cross-check: C&W H2 2025 table gave Sydney 189 MW UC + 1,102 MW planned = 1,291 MW, and 1,291 x 1.65 = 2,130 matches the stated +65%. Melbourne 127 MW is stated in Knight Frank/DC Byte Data Centre Atlas 2026 (https://www.knightfrank.co.uk/site-assets/research/report-pdfs/data-centres/data-centre-atlas-2026.pdf, Q2 2026: '443MW in Q2 2026, with a further 127MW under construction and 1.7GW committed'). Perth, Brisbane, Canberra not covered by either. Alternative bases: NEXTDC alone reports 537 MW under construction (ASX FY26, 27 Aug 2026, T1, company-wide fit-out, previous value in this field); Renewmap's May 2026 snapshot via ITK Research (https://itkservices3.com/background/data_centres_australia_top10_construction) counts 19 sites under construction totalling 1,853 MW, but on a full-campus master-plan basis (e.g. AirTrunk SYD3 400 MW), not phase IT load, so it is not comparable with C&W.

TNB's 23 projects / 3.8 GW under construction (1Q2026) is a facility maximum-demand basis and not comparable.

notes: REGIONAL ROW (2026-09-03). Under construction 4,764 MW is stated verbatim on Cushman & Wakefield's APAC Data Centre Update H1 2026 insights page: 'The pipeline now comprises 4,764MW under construction and 21,691MW in planning, while approximately 1,372MW of new operational capacity was delivered across the region' (pipeline 26,455 MW, +7,103 MW in H1 2026; vacancy 10.3%). Rounded to '4.8GW under-construction' in the 5 Aug 2026 press release (https://www.cushmanwakefield.com/en/singapore/news/2026/08/apac-dc-h1-2026). INCLUDES MAINLAND CHINA: the same page lists the report's primary markets as 'Tokyo, Singapore, Sydney, Mumbai, Hong Kong, China, Johor, Seoul, Jakarta, and Bangkok' and secondary markets 'Delhi, Taipei, Auckland, Manila, Ho Chi Minh City, and Perth'; the Japanese edition (https://www.cushmanwakefield.com/ja-jp/japan/insights/apac-data-centre-update) spells it out as 中国本土 (mainland China). C&W's Global Data Center Market Comparison 2026 (via DCD, 21 May 2026) confirms APAC operational 13.8 GW includes Beijing as the largest APAC market, and Mingtiandi (27 Mar 2026) quotes mainland China at 4.6 GW (39%) of end-2025 operational capacity. Prior reading: H2 2025 Update gave 3.7 GW under construction and 15.7 GW planned at end-2025 (https://www.cushmanwakefield.com/en/singapore/news/2026/03/apac-data-centre-development-pipeline-hits-record-in-2025). Live 13,800 MW is C&W's APAC operational capacity at end-2025 (includes China); H1 2026 total not stated (only +1,372 MW delivered). Per-country UC rows in this file sum to about 4,050 MW; the gap to 4,764 MW is mainland China (Beijing/Shanghai UC not public), Osaka, Perth, Delhi, HCMC and date mismatches (Tokyo/Hong Kong/Singapore rows are end-2025; India mid-2025; Taiwan mid-2025).
